newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Mar 11.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Mar 11.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Victorian Government is looking into plans prepared by management consultants Booz Allen & Hamilton to split the State's Public Transport Corp into at least seven separate State-owned corporations. The blueprint, which involves the creation of two seprate metropolitan rail operations and two separate tram operations, says the State Government should begin privatising as soon as possible. Page 1.

In a move which could lead to parts or all of the superannuation surcharge legislation overturned by a constitutional challenge in the High Court, New South Wales and South Australia have labelled the surcharge potentially unconstitutional. The South Australian Government says it may not co-operate with the Commonwealth's proposal for the surcharge. Page 3.

According to a media survey by Sydney-based analysing agency Computer Aided Research & Media Analysis, which studied 367 reports dealing with Asian issues appearing in major metropolitan newspapers during the race debate inspired by controversial Queenslad Independent Pauline Hanson, Australia's media was even-handed in its treatment of Asian issues. Page 3.

In a move soon to be followed by the rest of Australia's largest ticket sellers, BASS Online, a division of the Adelaide Festival Project, is soon to go live on the Internet. Computerised ticket seller BASS, which sells more than 1.4 million tickets a yea, is the first Australian ticket seller to make such a move. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Under the Federal Government's work-for-the-dole schemes, expected to be in place by the end of 1997 after a Cabinet meeting today, young people who refuse to work up to 20 hours a week on community-based projects could lose all their unemployment benefit. Prime Minister John Howard is expected to unveil details of the schemes after today's meeting. Page 1.

Following a five-hour meeting with Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan on the weekend, Prime Minister John Howard revealed yesterday Australia has offered Papua New Guinea additional aid and a boost in training for the PNG Defence Force in a bd to stop mercenaries being used to solve the Bougainville crisis. Page 1.

As the Queensland Government appears set to lift its controversial Wik-related freeze on land dealings, Prime Minister John Howard signalled yesterday farmers will have more access to legal aid to contest native title claims as part of the Coalition's resonse to the High Court's Wik ruling. Page 1.

The Australian Medical Association has supported a strike throughout New South Wales by 2,000 young doctors, along with stop-work meetings in most other States, to protest Federal Government plans to restrict Medicare provider numbers. A mass meeting of jnior doctors on Friday will decide whether to extend the strike action indefinitely. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

According to a leaked internal Australian Foreign Affairs assessment, China remains "totally unyielding" over human rights, and warns that any strong human rights stance by the Australian Government might result in China challenging Australia's role in Asa, including its bid to attend the Asia-Europe Meeting in December. Page 1.

Rockhampton regional co-ordinator of the Queensland Emergency Services Department Mike Morrison says Cyclone Justin, the biggest cyclone to threaten Queensland for more than 20 years, is lashing at the State's entire north coast, threatening homes, sweepig away beaches and forcing the closure of ports. Page 1.

Ending more than 150 years of debate on the spelling of Australia's largest mountain, the eight-member Geographical Names Board announced yesterday Mount Kosciusko is to known as Mount Kosciuszko, with the spelling now including the "z" missing since 1840 Page 1.

New South Wales hospital services were in chaos last night, as sympathetic senior doctors refused to cover work missed by 2,000 striking junior doctors. Elective surgery was put on hold and outpatient clinics closed, yet the Howard Government is refusingto back the demands of the striking doctors for greater access to Medicare. Page 1.
THE AGE

After Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett's warning yesterday that unions would pay heavily for the weekend transport strikes, Trades Hall Council secretary Leigh Hubbard foreshadowed massive union opposition to any State Government plans to sell tram, train ad bus services. Page 1.

With a Budget less than half of its New South Wales counterpart, the Victorian Environment Protection Authority is under-resourced for its ever-increasing workload and appears to be failing in key areas of its role as a watchdog for Melbourne's air polluton. Air quality standards have not been updated for 16 years. Page 1.

According to figures from the Department of Employment, Education, Training and Youth Affairs, unemployment is worsening in parts of Melbourne and regional Victoria. The most dramatic changes occured north and north-east of the Yarra, where average emploment jumped from 8.8 per cent in 1995 to 11.4 per cent last year. Page 1.

Following objections from the Australian Government and industry groups including the Australian Meat and Livestock Corporation, South Korea yesterday cleared three consignments of Australian processed meat and milk products, which had been held on wharve since February 26 after being quarantined because of anthrax concerns. Page 1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
